programme.title: The Secret World of Haute Couture
programme.desc: Margy Kinmonth meets millionaire customers and world-famous designers as she explores the anachronistic but little-explained pocket of the fashion industry known as haute couture.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo is on the last leg of his railway journey from the train-building city of Derby to the aircraft manufacturing base of Filton. From Tewkesbury, he heads to the fairytale castle of Eastnor at the foot of the Malvern Hills.

programme.title: Gareth Edwards' Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: Sir Gareth and wife Maureen get a castle to themselves for a night, perfect to mark their 49th wedding anniversary. Plus they go wildlife spotting and get competitive at golf in Tenby.

programme.title: City Scapes
programme.desc: Post-war architectural innovations in the Big Apple.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Celia Imrie tells the story behind one of the most groundbreaking and influential films of the sixties, 1967's Bonnie and Clyde, starring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway.

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis tells the story of the English ruler who left the most indelible mark on the castle - the great Plantagenet king, Edward I who turned it into an instrument of colonisation.

programme.title: Meet the Ancestors
programme.desc: John visits a couple in Gunner, near Salisbury, who wanted to build a garage next to their bungalow but did not realise they were living by a fifth-century graveyard. The programme follows a team of archaeologists as they excavate off the skeleton of a 30-year-old man, attempting to resolve whether he was a Saxon or a native Briton.

programme.title: The Good Old Days

programme.title: Hetty Wainthropp Investigates
programme.desc: It's the 50th anniversary of the Blainthorp Music Festival and there is fierce competition to be chosen as Golden Voice. Suddenly, the finalists start losing their voices and Hetty must find out why.

programme.title: The Turkish Detective
programme.desc: Detective Mehmet Suleyman arrives in Istanbul to join the formidable Inspector Cetin Ikmen's homicide unit, alongside Detective Ayse Farsakoglu and IT guru Tarik, and finds himself embroiled in his first murder investigation.

programme.title: The Turkish Detective
programme.desc: With the new development on Gozde's case, suspicion initially falls on her secret boyfriend Kemal. However, after Kemal's interrogation, and the non-confirmation of another man's alibi, a new suspect is formed.

programme.title: Wogan
programme.sub-title: Jenny Agutter, Laurie Lee, John Garnett
programme.desc: Terry Wogan's guests are Jenny Agutter, Laurie Lee, who recites a piece from As I Walked Out One Midsummer Morning, and John Garnett. Barbara Dickson sings The Right Moment.

programme.title: Comic Roots
programme.desc: Kenneth Williams explores his roots in and around London's St Pancras, where he grew up. Architecture, poetry, art and music were the formative influences on Kenneth Williams: the slum architecture of St Pancras where he grew up; the liquid poetry of his gran's fruity anecdotes; the art of the Marcel wave practised by his hairdresser father; and the musical knees-up of `The Boot'.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Aston Hall in Birmingham, where treasures include some rare trading beads, memorable items from an Aston Villa legend and a collection of climbing gear from one of history's great mountaineers. Expert Will Farmer meets local man and celebrated poet Benjamin Zephaniah, who has brought along his own intriguing collection, and Fiona explores the Civil War-era history of the hall.

programme.title: British History's Biggest Fibs with Lucy Worsley
programme.desc: Lucy debunks the `Glorious Revolution'. In 1688, the British Isles were invaded by a huge army led by Dutch prince, William of Orange. With his English wife Mary he stole the throne from Mary's father, the Catholic King James II. This was the death knell for absolute royal power and laid the foundations of our constitutional monarchy.
